title: Broken Retaining Wall
description: A thick limestone retaining wall with a central collapse, fractured ashlar, exposed rubble core and a debris fan.

review.notes: Rebuild round 2 of 2 (last): rejected. Fixed: the wall now carries a weathering gradient: darker damp lower courses, grey-green lichen flecks on faces and tops, varied block tones, and a few chipped corners (hero, closeup_base). Still failing: (1) form_detail/defects 7: the exposed rubble core is still a pile of small, pale, sharp-edged cubes stacked in the breaks (closeup upper left and right, closeup_base upper right), with no dark lime mortar between them, so it reads as sugar cubes, not a rubble-and-mortar core. (2) material 7: the fallen blocks in the breach are clean, flat-faced boxes and wedges with even, decal-like lichen dots; the upper courses stay clean pale grey with no rain streaks under the broken tops. (3) defects 7: the turf patches are flat, smooth discs with hard rounded edges lying on the ground (closeup_base lower left and right). Fix: fill the core with dark grey-brown mortar and embed mixed rounded and broken stones in it; spall and round the fallen blocks and break their faces; add rain streaks below the broken tops; blend the turf into the ground with an irregular, tufted edge.
